title: The Representation Problem: 0.999... as Engineering Convention, Not Mathematical Identity
abstract: The standard mathematical claim that 0.999... = 1 is widely accepted and supported by multiple proof methods within real analysis. This paper argues that the claim is not a valid equality in the strict sense that mathematics defines equality. Instead, it is a type coercion between a base-dependent series function and a base-independent number. The limit convention that resolves the gap between these two objects is an engineering solution to a deficiency in base-10 positional encoding. It is not a mathematical property derivable from first principles. The paper further argues that positional notation itself embeds base-10 assumptions into all bases, making cross-base verification of such claims circular.
